title: Codimension-two intersection supplies independent generic linear combinations
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] which is an integral domain. Let $n\geq2$ and $g_1,\ldots,g_n\in A$. Suppose the closed subset $V(g_1,g_2)\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] has an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of dimension $\dim(A)-2$, with dimension the Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ for the field of fractions. Then there exist $c_1,\ldots,c_n\in k$ such that $x_1,\ldots,x_n,\sum_{i=1}^n g_ix_i,\sum_{i=1}^n c_ig_i$ are algebraically independent over $k$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree] in $K(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\operatorname{Frac}(K[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Here $V(g_1,g_2)$ consists of the prime ideals containing both elements.

proof.text: Put $h=\sum_{i=1}^n g_i x_i$, $C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $B=k[X_1,\ldots,X_n,Y,Z]$. These are finite type $k$-algebras: adjoining the finitely many variables to a finite generating set for $A$ gives a generating set for $C$. The polynomial universal property defines $\varphi:B\to C$ by $X_i\mapsto x_i$, $Y\mapsto h$, $Z\mapsto g_2$. The ring $C$ is a domain: order monomials lexicographically and the largest monomial in a product of two nonzero polynomials has coefficient the product of their largest coefficients, which is nonzero in $A$. The maps $A\hookrightarrow K$, $A[x]\hookrightarrow K[x]\hookrightarrow K(x)$ are injective (coefficientwise for the polynomial map, and by the definition of the fraction field). Thus a polynomial relation over $k$ among $x_1,\ldots,x_n,h,g_2$ in $K(x)$ is exactly an element of $\ker\varphi$. It suffices to prove $\ker\varphi=0$.

source.place: Tag 0G4E, lemma-algebraically-independent, proof; first paragraph, affine presentation and independence as injectivity

proof.text: Write $d=\dim A$. The finite-type-domain dimension theorem shows that $d$ is a finite nonnegative integer. The finite-type Noetherianity theorem applies to $A$ and to $k$ (generated over itself by the empty set). Hence the polynomial dimension theorem gives $\dim C=d+n$ and $\dim B=n+2$: the only prime ideal of the field $k$ is $(0)$, so $\dim k=0$.

source.place: Tag 0G4E, lemma-algebraically-independent, proof; dimension calculation preceding the fibre inequality

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak m=(X_1-1,X_2,\ldots,X_n,Y,Z)\subset B$. Evaluation at $(1,0,\ldots,0,0,0)$ gives $B/\mathfrak m\cong k$, so $\mathfrak m$ is a rational maximal ideal. Its extended ideal is $J=(x_1-1,x_2,\ldots,x_n,h,g_2)\subset C$. The identity $h-g_1=g_1(x_1-1)+\sum_{i=2}^n g_ix_i$ proves $J=(x_1-1,x_2,\ldots,x_n,g_1,g_2)$. Evaluation $x_1\mapsto1$, $x_i\mapsto0$ for $i\geq2$, followed by $A\to A/(g_1,g_2)$, and the inclusion of constants modulo $J$ are inverse maps $C/J\cong A/(g_1,g_2)$. The induced homeomorphism of spectra identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$ with $V(g_1,g_2)$: a prime of $A/(g_1,g_2)$ corresponds to its inverse image in $A$, a prime containing both generators. It preserves irreducible components and chains of irreducible closed subsets. Thus the hypothesis supplies an irreducible component $W$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$ with $\dim W=d-2$. In particular this fibre is nonempty and $d\geq2$.

source.place: Tag 0G4E, lemma-algebraically-independent, proof; last paragraph, the displayed fibre equations

proof.text: Suppose $P=\ker\varphi\neq0$. It is a proper prime ideal because $C$ is a domain and $\varphi$ is unital. The polynomial ring $B$ over $k$ is also a domain. Any strict chain of primes of $B/P$ pulls back to a strict chain of primes of $B$ all containing the nonzero ideal $P$. Prepending the strictly smaller prime $(0)$ increases its length by one. Since $\dim B=n+2$, this proves $\dim(B/P)\leq n+1$. These dimensions are ordinary finite integers: $B/P$ is a nonzero finite type domain, and its dimension is bounded by the same chain argument.

source.place: Tag 0G4E, lemma-algebraically-independent, proof; first paragraph, dimension drop for a nondominant map

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-finite-type-fibre-component-lower-bound] to the finite type $k$-algebras $B,C$, the homomorphism $\varphi$, and the rational maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of Step 3. The domain hypothesis for $C$ was verified in Step 1. Its ideal $J$ is exactly the extended ideal computed in Step 3. Hence that statement applies to the particular irreducible component $W$ supplied by the hypothesis, and yields $d-2=\dim W\geq\dim C-\dim(B/P)\geq(d+n)-(n+1)=d-1$, a contradiction. Consequently $\ker\varphi=0$.

source.place: Tag 0G4E, lemma-algebraically-independent, proof; first paragraph fibre lower bound and final paragraph contradiction

proof.text: Choose $c_2=1$ and $c_i=0$ for $i\neq2$, which is permitted since $n\geq2$. Then $\sum_i c_i g_i=g_2$. By Step 1 and $\ker\varphi=0$, no nonzero polynomial over $k$ vanishes on $x_1,\ldots,x_n,\sum_i g_ix_i,g_2$ in $K(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$. This is precisely the required algebraic independence. The choice uses only $0,1\in k$, so the argument also applies when $k$ is finite.
